cards.text: Isaiah the prophet is speaking for the LORD, and Zion, another name for Jerusalem, is pictured as a woman. Heaven and earth were just told to sing for joy (Isaiah 49:13), but Zion's not singing. She says, "The LORD has forsaken me; the Lord has forgotten me!"

cards.question: The LORD answers Zion with a question about a mother. What does He ask if a woman can forget?
The LORD says that even if a mother could forget her child, He still will not forget Zion.

cards.text: Then the LORD says He has inscribed Zion on the palms of His hands. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer feeling forgotten, and nobody wrote me down on ANYTHING, not even a sticky note.

cards.question: Zion is inscribed on the palms of the LORD's hands. What does that picture show?

cards.text: Her walls are ever before Him. And the destroyers and wreckers who tore her down? They're packing up and leaving.

cards.question: As Zion's destroyers depart, her ___ hurry back.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells her, "Lift up your eyes and look around." Zion thought nobody was coming, and now there's a whole CROWD gathering and heading her way.

cards.question: The LORD swears by His own life that Zion will wear this crowd as ___ and put them on like a ___.
The LORD says Zion's ruined and desolate land will now be too small for her people.

cards.text: Those who devoured her will be far away, and the children of her bereavement will say, "This place is too small for us; make room for us to live here." Friend, that's the kind of complaint you WANT, when your place is so full of family nobody can find a seat.

cards.question: Zion was bereaved and barren, exiled and left all alone. When she sees all these children, what does she do in her heart?

answers.text: She wonders where they came from
She tells them all to move out
She sends them back to the nations

cards.text: Then the Lord GOD answers her wondering: "Behold, I will lift up My hand to the nations, and raise My banner to the peoples." That's a signal, friend, and the whole world can see it.

cards.question: When the LORD raises His banner to the nations, what do they do with Zion's sons and daughters?

answers.text: They carry them back to her

cards.question: The LORD says kings will be Zion's foster ___, and their queens her nursing ___.

cards.text: Those kings will bow to her facedown and lick the dust at her feet. Zion went from forgotten to kings on the floor, and I went from the back of a junk drawer to my own PLANET, so friend, never count yourself out.

cards.question: The LORD says Zion will know that He is the LORD. What does He promise those who hope in Him?

answers.text: They will never be put to shame

cards.text: Then comes a question: "Can the plunder be snatched from the mighty, or the captives of a tyrant be delivered?" That's like trying to get your phone charger back from your boss, and friend, that charger is GONE.

cards.question: The LORD says even the captives of the mighty will be taken away from them.
The LORD promises to save Zion's children. Who does He say He will contend with?

answers.text: The kings who carry her sons

cards.text: Then the LORD says He will make Zion's oppressors eat their own flesh, and they will be drunk on their own blood, as with wine.

cards.question: When it's all done, only Zion will know that the LORD is her Savior and Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.

findings.problem: The card says Zion is 'another name for Jerusalem.' This fact comes from outside the passage, and the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This question asks which thing a woman can forget. The wrong answers 'Her own name' and 'Her wedding day' are made-up items, not real details from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: 'Zion thought nobody was coming' gives Zion a thought the text never states. It is told as fact, not marked as Papa Dorin's own guess. In v14 Zion says the LORD has forsaken and forgotten her. She says nothing about anyone coming.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The two blanks ask the baker to guess the exact wording of v18 ('jewelry' and 'bride'). Nothing on the earlier cards lets a baker reason out these words over 'armor' or 'chains,' so the card tests unseen wording, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: 'Then the Lord GOD answers her wondering' states that v22 is a reply to Zion's questions in v21. The text doesn't make that link. 'The whole world can see it' also goes beyond 'the nations' and 'the peoples.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Zion went from forgotten' says Zion really was forgotten. The passage says the opposite: the LORD answers 'I will not forget you!' (v15). Zion only said she was forgotten (v14). The joke also lands as a pep-talk moral ('never count yourself out') rather than a real laugh.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: 'When it's all done' adds a time frame the text doesn't give. Verse 26 only says 'Then all mankind will know.'

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.
